description: Curated historical Accra flood events for backtesting the ThirdWave geospatial vulnerability grid and seeding a demo of the CitizenReport -> Incident operational loop. NOT crowdsourced/live citizen data -- hindsight-curated from public news/reference sources, geocoded via OpenStreetMap Nominatim. Locations left ungeocoded where sources did not name a specific, unambiguous site rather than guessing.

events.name: Kwame Nkrumah Circle flood and fuel station explosion
events.deaths: over 200 (flood + GOIL fuel station explosion combined, per contemporary reporting)
events.cause: Heavy rainfall, choked drainage/gutters, floodwater carried petrol from a filling station which ignited

events.name: 2016 Accra floods
events.location_name: Accra (city-wide, no specific site named in source)
events.geocode_confidence: none - source does not name a specific location
events.cause: Heavy rainfall; streets flooded within 6 hours of rain

events.name: March 2023 Accra flood
events.cause: Rain-bearing cloud system over southeastern Ghana; inadequate drainage
events.note: Independent confirmation of the same Circle/Odaw corridor hotspot flooding again 8 years after the 2015 disaster.

events.name: Ashaiman flood
events.geocode_source: OpenStreetMap Nominatim (town centre, not exact bridge sites)
events.geocode_confidence: medium - town centre used; source names specific destroyed bridges (Valco Flat, Ashaiman Lebanon, Roman Down) not individually geocoded
events.cause: Over 12 hours of continuous heavy downpour

events.name: Weija Dam spillage flood
events.location_name: Weija, Greater Accra (also affected: Ashalaja, Oblogo, Tetegu)
events.geocode_confidence: high for Weija; Ashalaja/Oblogo could not be confidently geocoded and are not plotted
events.displaced: approx. 1,500 (approx. 1,000 houses flooded); NADMO separately estimated ~2,000 directly affected; a later fact-check roundup cites 500 displaced as "highest in the dam's history" -- displacement figures are genuinely inconsistent across sources, not reconciled here.
events.cause: Prolonged heavy rainfall raised Weija Dam level to 49.5ft (max operating level 48ft); Ghana Water Company opened 4 spill gates
events.note: Weija flooded again in May 2025 (see WEIJA-FLOOD-2025-05) -- recurring hotspot, same pattern as Kwame Nkrumah Circle.
events.deaths_note: Addi Kwashie (also spelled Kwashe Addi), 55, a truck pusher, found dead in a flooded room at Tetegu on Thursday Oct 6 2022 -- drowned after seeking refuge in an abandoned building (Graphic Online, Ghanaian Times, Citi Newsroom, MyJoyOnline all corroborate age/location/cause).

events.name: May 2025 Accra storm flood
events.location_name: Weija, Greater Accra (also affected region-wide: Ofankor Barrier, Kaneshie, Labadi, Adentan-Dodowa, parts of Tema)
events.geocode_source: OpenStreetMap Nominatim (Weija used as anchor; other affected areas not individually geocoded -- multi-site regional event)
events.geocode_confidence: medium - regional event, Weija is one of several named affected areas

events.name: May 2026 Kaneshie flood
events.cause: Heavy downpour; also affected Kpone Barrier and Santa Maria
events.note: No casualties reported for this event -- vehicles stranded and major roads gridlocked. Kaneshie (Ablekuma Central Municipal) is inside the pilot district and floods repeatedly (see also ACCRA-FLOOD-2026-06-29).

events.name: June 2026 Accra floods
events.location_name: Kwame Nkrumah Circle, Accra (regional event -- also affected Alajo, Adabraka, Kaneshie, Weija, Tse Addo, Ofankor, Pantang, Ashongman Estates, parts of Tema)
events.geocode_source: OpenStreetMap Nominatim (Circle used as anchor; other named areas not individually geocoded -- multi-site regional event, see ALAJO-FLOOD-2026-06-29 for one that is)
events.geocode_confidence: medium - regional event, Circle is one of several named affected areas
events.displaced: 7,761 households (3,882 people) per Ghana News Agency; other contemporary reports cited up to 48,000 displaced
events.cause: Torrential rainfall described by officials as one of the heaviest to hit Accra in recent years
events.note: GNFS reported 150+ people rescued. Lectures/exams suspended at some tertiary institutions; GRIDCo/ECG cut power from Mallam and Achimota substations as a precaution.

events.name: Alajo electrocution deaths (June 2026 Accra floods)
events.cause: Floodwater entered homes and contacted electrical installations; part of the same June 29, 2026 storm as ACCRA-FLOOD-2026-06-29
events.note: OSM/Nominatim labels this area's district as 'Ayawaso Central Municipal', but it falls inside our own pilot_district_assemblies.geojson polygon for Ablekuma North Municipal -- used the latter (our authoritative boundary) for district assignment, consistent with how the rest of this project resolves district membership.

events.name: 2023 Akosombo/Kpong Dam spillage
events.location_name: Mepe, North Tongu District, Volta Region (also affected: Central/South Tongu, Asuogyaman District (Eastern Region), Tefle, Wume, Sokpoe; Alikekope, Agorme, Agbave reported as having 'completely disappeared')
events.geocode_source: OpenStreetMap Nominatim (Mepe used as anchor -- 'most affected' per Wikipedia -- other named communities not individually geocoded)
events.geocode_confidence: medium - regional event spanning multiple districts, Mepe is one of several named affected areas
events.cause: Sustained heavy 2023 rainfall raised the Akosombo reservoir above its 276ft maximum operating level; VRA began controlled spillage at both Akosombo and Kpong dams on 2023-09-15, intensified 2023-10-09, flooding communities downstream on the Volta River
events.note: OUTSIDE both the pilot district and the 4-district extended coverage (Volta/Eastern Region, not Greater Accra) -- included as a reference dam-release event, not a location this project scores. Same hazard_type as the Weija events below; useful for the AI Assistant to recognize dam-release flooding as a distinct pattern from urban/flash flooding, even where it can't provide a zone score for the location.

events.name: May 2026 Weija Dam spillage flood
events.location_name: Tetegu, Weija Gbawe Municipal (also affected: Ashbread, Kinshasha, White Cross, Oblogo, Tatop)
events.geocode_confidence: high for Tetegu; other named communities not individually geocoded
events.displaced: hundreds of homes flooded; Regional Security Council (REGSEC) ordered evacuation of all downstream communities
events.cause: Ghana Water Limited opened all spill gates 2026-05-27 after the dam's water level exceeded 48ft. Contested cause worth keeping both sides of: GWL itself publicly attributed the resulting FLOODING (not the spillage decision) to illegal structures and waterway encroachment rather than the spillage alone -- directly consistent with this project's own channel-encroachment findings (see channel_encroachment_index.py).
events.note: Third documented Weija dam-release flood in this file (see WEIJA-DAM-FLOOD-2022-10-04, WEIJA-FLOOD-2025-05) -- a genuinely recurring hazard, not a one-off. This is the only event in this file where an official source explicitly names encroachment/illegal structures as a contributing cause rather than just 'heavy rain'.

events.name: September 2026 Weija Dam spillage flood
events.location_name: Tetegu, Oblogo, Weija (also affected: Pambros Salt, Lower McCarthy Hill, Lower Weija, Bojo Beach, Ada Kopey)
events.geocode_source: OpenStreetMap Nominatim (reused Tetegu coordinate from WEIJA-DAM-FLOOD-2026-05-27 -- same community)
events.geocode_confidence: high for Tetegu; other named communities not individually geocoded
events.displaced: homes and roads submerged by the Densu overflowing its banks; residents fled, some using canoes to move belongings
events.cause: Ghana Water Limited resumed controlled spillage 2026-09-09 after the dam water level rose to 45.2ft (near the 46ft threshold) following heavy rain upstream in the Densu River catchment. GWL warned 8 communities to evacuate ahead of the spillage (statement dated 2026-09-07).
events.note: Fourth documented Weija dam-release flood in this file (see WEIJA-DAM-FLOOD-2022-10-04, WEIJA-FLOOD-2025-05, WEIJA-DAM-FLOOD-2026-05-27) -- confirms this is a recurring, near-annual hazard, now twice in the same year (May and September 2026). In response, a $350m flood-control project (levee canal from the dam to the Atlantic, with a permanent estuary) was announced to begin December 2026 (citinewsroom.com/2026/09/weija-dam-spillage-350m-flood-control-project-to-begin-by-december).

events.name: New Juaben North (Akwadum) Densu River flood
events.location_name: Akwadum, New Juaben North Municipal (also affected: New Juaben South Municipal/Koforidua, Denkyembour, Akyemansa -- wider Eastern Region event, Sept 30-Oct 3 2022, 17 MMDAs affected)
events.geocode_source: OpenStreetMap Nominatim (Akwadum Feeder Road, New Juaben North Municipal District -- road geocode, not a settlement centroid)
events.geocode_confidence: medium -- anchors to Akwadum itself, other named districts not individually geocoded
events.deaths_note: 5 deaths across 4 Eastern Region districts that weekend (New Juaben North 2, New Juaben South 1, Denkyembour 1, Akyemansa 1); separately 10 people declared missing in Nsawam-Adoagyiri Municipal (different district, not New Juaben)
events.displaced: 45 mud houses collapsed at Akwadum; 1,448 people recorded affected in Asokore per the New Juaben North Municipal Assembly situational report; hundreds displaced regionally
events.cause: Heavy rainfall Sept 30-Oct 3 2022 caused the Densu River (also Birem and Ayensu rivers elsewhere in the region) to overflow its banks. The local MP specifically attributed worsened flooding to illegal mining (galamsey) upstream of Koforidua, and called for a drainage system review. The Akwadum bridge over the Densu was among the worst-hit infrastructure.
events.note: Upstream, same-basin counterpart to the Weija Dam spillage floods already documented in this file (WEIJA-DAM-FLOOD-2022-10-04, WEIJA-FLOOD-2025-05, WEIJA-DAM-FLOOD-2026-05-27, WEIJA-DAM-FLOOD-2026-09-09): the Densu River rises in the Atewa Range near Kibi, flows through the Akwadum/Koforidua area, then south to the Weija reservoir near Accra -- same river, ~110km apart. Galamsey-driven upstream land degradation near Koforidua is a plausible but UNVERIFIED contributing factor to downstream Weija inflow/sedimentation -- flagged as a real hydrological connection worth investigating, not an established causal claim. New Juaben itself is well outside ThirdWave's pilot district, extended coverage, and Lower Volta region -- not modelled by any existing coverage, added here for the record only.

events.name: June 2014 Weija Dam spillage flood
events.geocode_confidence: date is month-only (Wikipedia gives no day); not geocoded
events.cause: Weija Dam spillage flooded Glefe; residents blamed the Bortianor Traditional Council for refusing to allow dredging of the river draining to the sea until after the Homowo festival concluded.
events.note: Predates both Sentinel-1 (launched April 2014, operational ~Oct 2014) and Sentinel-2 (launched June 2015) -- no satellite imagery of any kind exists for this event from either mission.

events.name: March 2017 Weija Dam spillage flood
events.geocode_source: OpenStreetMap Nominatim (Tetegu, reused from later Weija events -- same community)
events.geocode_confidence: date is month-only (Wikipedia gives no day)
events.cause: Ghana Water Company spilled water to keep the reservoir below its rainy-season maximum operating limit.
events.note: Both Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 were operational by March 2017 (S1B launched Apr 2016, S2B launched Mar 2017) -- archive coverage should exist, unlike the 2014 event.

events.name: October 2020 Weija Dam spillage flood
events.location_name: Tetegu, Oblogo, Pambros Salt, Lower McCarthy Hill, Lower Weija, Bojo Beach, Ada Kopey and surrounding communities
events.geocode_source: OpenStreetMap Nominatim (Tetegu, reused -- same community as other Weija events)
events.geocode_confidence: high for date (GWCL press release + Citi Newsroom both confirm Sunday Oct 11 2020); Tetegu anchor only, other named communities not individually geocoded
events.cause: Heavy rain in the Densu catchment raised the dam from 46.8ft to 48.4ft in under 24 hours (above the 47ft safe operating level); GWCL began spillage Sunday Oct 11 2020. A 2024 peer-reviewed study (Jamba journal) describes this specifically as "particularly devastating" among the dam's repeated floods -- 10% of surveyed residents in that study reported losing a family member in it.
events.note: The most severe of the pre-2022 events by the academic source's own characterization -- worth prioritizing for satellite change-detection given both missions were fully operational.

events.name: March 2021 Weija Dam spillage flood
events.geocode_source: OpenStreetMap Nominatim (Weija, reused from the Oct 2022 event)
events.geocode_confidence: date is month-only (Wikipedia gives no day); location anchored to Weija itself, not confirmed to a specific downstream community
events.cause: Water level rose 1.9ft in 24 hours (46.2 to 48.1ft, 1.1ft above the 47ft safe operating level); gates opened to guard against collapse risk.
events.note: Both missions operational; month-only date limits SAR/optical before-during-after precision the way it worked for later, day-dated events.
